grade.rationale: The stylesheet is generally coherent and uses shared design tokens effectively, but its hotspot table is not viable on narrow mobile viewports because minimum column widths exceed the available space while overflow is clipped.

summary: The dashboard styling is mostly correct and consistently organized. One responsive-layout defect can hide hotspot data on small screens. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable due to missing dependencies.

grade.rationale: Most layouts have responsive adjustments, but the hotspot table remains at least 512px wide on the narrow breakpoint and clips overflowing columns.
Selectors are logically grouped and predominantly use shared tokens, though densely packed declarations make future modifications and reviews somewhat harder.
Class names communicate intent well, but multiple complete rules on single lines reduce readability and make changes harder to isolate.
The stylesheet provides distinct error, retry, refresh, and loading-state presentation. Functional recovery behavior cannot be assessed from CSS alone.

The component-oriented selectors are amenable to visual and viewport testing, but no coverage evidence is available and the narrow-screen clipping case indicates a missing responsive regression check.

findings.title: Hotspot columns are clipped on narrow mobile viewports
findings.description: At the 900px breakpoint, the five columns still require at least 464px, plus 32px of grid gaps and 20px of horizontal padding, for a total minimum width of 516px. On common mobile viewports the grid therefore overflows its container, while the container's `overflow:hidden` clips the excess. Users can lose access to the right-hand hotspot fields because no horizontal scrolling or alternative compact layout is provided.
findings.recommendation: At a smaller breakpoint, replace the row with a stacked or reduced-column layout. If retaining the table structure, wrap it in a container with `overflow-x:auto` instead of clipping it, and add visual regression tests at representative widths such as 320px and 375px.
